title: Chebyshev's θ function bounded: θ(n) ≤ n·log 4 via the primorial / central-binomial sandwich
description: A fully machine-checked, axiom-free derivation of the upper Chebyshev bound on the first Chebyshev function θ(n) = ∑_{p ≤ n, p prime} log p. The key observation is that the exponential of θ(n) is exactly the primorial n# = ∏_{p ≤ n} p, so θ(n) = log(n#). Mathlib packages the Erdős central-binomial sandwich as Nat.primorial_le_4_pow : n# ≤ 4ⁿ; taking logarithms and using monotonicity of log on the positive reals turns this into θ(n) ≤ n·log 4 = 2n·log 2, the upper half of the classical Chebyshev estimates on θ. This is the θ-level companion to the parent's central-binomial coefficient sandwich (chebyshev-bounds-oq-06): where the parent bounds C(2n,n), this entry bounds the prime-log sum θ that C(2n,n) controls.

sections.title: θ(n) as the logarithm of the primorial

sections.title: θ is nonnegative and monotone

sections.title: The upper Chebyshev bound θ(n) ≤ n·log 4
sections.summary: chebyshevTheta_le rewrites θ(n) = log(n#), applies Real.log_le_log to the primorial bound n# ≤ 4ⁿ (Nat.primorial_le_4_pow), and finishes with Real.log_pow: log(4ⁿ) = n·log 4. chebyshevTheta_le_two_mul restates this as θ(n) ≤ 2n·log 2 via log 4 = 2·log 2.

overview.historicalContext: Chebyshev's first function θ(x) = ∑_{p ≤ x} log p, introduced by Pafnuty Chebyshev around 1850, is the additive prime-counting weight that sits at the analytic heart of the prime number theorem. Decades before Hadamard and de la Vallée Poussin proved the PNT in 1896, Chebyshev showed by elementary means that θ(x) grows linearly: there are explicit constants $a, b > 0$ with $a\,x \le \theta(x) \le b\,x$ for large $x$. The clean upper constant $b = \log 4 = 2\log 2$ comes from the Erdős-style estimate on the primorial $n\# = \prod_{p \le n} p$ — the same central-binomial argument that underlies Bertrand's postulate. This entry formalizes exactly that upper half in its cleanest form.
overview.problemStatement: Let $\theta(n) = \sum_{p \le n,\ p\text{ prime}} \log p$ be the first Chebyshev function. The claim is the upper bound $\theta(n) \le n \log 4$ for every natural number $n$, equivalently $\theta(n) \le 2n \log 2$. This is the upper side of Chebyshev's classical two-sided estimate $\theta(n) = \Theta(n)$.
overview.proofStrategy: The engine is a single identity: exponentiating θ(n) turns the additive prime sum into a multiplicative product, since $\sum_{p \le n} \log p = \log \prod_{p \le n} p$, giving $\theta(n) = \log(n\#)$. Mathlib already contains the arithmetic heart — `primorial_le_4_pow : n# ≤ 4ⁿ`, whose own proof is the Erdős argument bounding the primorial by a central binomial coefficient $\binom{2m}{m}$. Taking logarithms of $n\# \le 4^n$ and using that log is increasing on the positive reals (with $n\# > 0$ from `primorial_pos`) yields $\theta(n) = \log(n\#) \le \log(4^n) = n \log 4$ immediately. The Lean development supplies the log-side packaging: it defines θ, proves the bridge identity $\theta(n) = \log(n\#)$ by casting the ℕ-product to ℝ and applying `Real.log_prod`, and then reads off the Chebyshev estimate via `Real.log_pow`.
keyInsights: Exponentiating an additive prime sum turns it into a multiplicative product: $\exp(\theta(n)) = \prod_{p \le n} p = n\#$, so $\theta(n) = \log(n\#)$. This single identity converts an analytic bound on θ into an arithmetic bound on the primorial.
The arithmetic content is entirely Mathlib's `primorial_le_4_pow` ($n\# \le 4^n$); the entry adds no new number theory, only the honest log-side translation into the standard θ statement.

The constant $\log 4 = 2\log 2$ is not arbitrary: it is the logarithm of the base 4 in the central-binomial bound $\prod_{p \le n} p \le 4^n$, the same estimate that powers Erdős's proof of Bertrand's postulate.
Monotonicity of log on $\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ is the only analytic input beyond the identity; positivity of the primorial is exactly what licenses taking logarithms.

Only the upper Chebyshev bound follows this cheaply. The matching lower bound $\theta(n) \ge c\,n$ is genuinely harder — it needs a lower estimate on how many primes lie below $n$, not just an upper product bound.

conclusion.summary: The upper Chebyshev bound $\theta(n) \le n \log 4 = 2n \log 2$ is verified in Lean 4 with 0 axioms and 0 sorries. The proof reduces the analytic statement to Mathlib's primorial bound $n\# \le 4^n$ via the identity $\theta(n) = \log(n\#)$ and monotonicity of the logarithm.
conclusion.implications: This is the upper half of Chebyshev's two-sided estimate $\theta(n) = \Theta(n)$, the elementary precursor to the prime number theorem. It sits directly above the parent central-binomial sandwich (chebyshev-bounds-oq-06): the primorial bound $n\# \le 4^n$ that this entry logarithmizes is proved in Mathlib from exactly the central binomial coefficient estimate the parent packages. Formalizing θ and its relation to the primorial gives a reusable handle on prime-counting sums for downstream analytic number theory.
openQuestions: Can the matching lower bound $\theta(n) \ge c\,n$ for an explicit constant $c > 0$ be formalized? This requires a positive-density input — a lower bound on the number of primes up to $n$, e.g. from the prime factorization of the central binomial coefficient $\binom{2n}{n}$.
Combining the two bounds would give the full two-sided Chebyshev estimate $\theta(n) = \Theta(n)$; is there a clean Lean statement packaging both constants?

Chebyshev's second function $\psi(x) = \sum_{p^k \le x} \log p$ differs from θ by a lower-order $O(\sqrt{x}\log^2 x)$ term; can the θ bound here be transferred to ψ to connect with the von Mangoldt / PNT formulation?
